tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

schema.name: Workflow
schema.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

"""Creates the neon material of the stand-ins (T-027). Runs inside the editor, headless:

UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe JamGame.uproject -run=pythonscript -script="Tools/Editor/create_neon_material.py"

M_JamNeon is unlit: its colour is all emission, Color times Glow, so a Glow above 1 blooms. An existing material is
left alone.
"""
import unreal

FOLDER = "/Game/Materials"
NAME = "M_JamNeon"
PATH = "%s/%s" % (FOLDER, NAME)

if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(PATH):
    unreal.log("create_neon_material: %s already exists" % PATH)
else:
    lib = unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary
    mat = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().create_asset(NAME, FOLDER, unreal.Material, unreal.MaterialFactoryNew())
    mat.set_editor_property("shading_model", unreal.MaterialShadingModel.MSM_UNLIT)
    color = lib.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionVectorParameter, -600, 0)
    color.set_editor_property("parameter_name", "Color")
    color.set_editor_property("default_value", unreal.LinearColor(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0))
    glow = lib.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionScalarParameter, -600, 250)
    glow.set_editor_property("parameter_name", "Glow")
    glow.set_editor_property("default_value", 1.0)
    times = lib.create_material_expression(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, -300, 100)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(color, "", times, "A")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(glow, "", times, "B")
    lib.connect_material_property(times, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_EMISSIVE_COLOR)
    lib.recompile_material(mat)
    saved = unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset(PATH, only_if_is_dirty=False)
    unreal.log("create_neon_material: %s saved=%s" % (PATH, saved))

content.content:
# C++ standard of the jam project

Ported from the CastleFight and Diskworld standards before the jam start. It holds working conventions only: no
game design. A new rule is added here only by the author's decision.

## Style

- Epic C++ Coding Standard + `.clang-format` in the root: tabs, Allman, braces always, `ColumnLimit: 140`.
  `check_code.py` checks the format, never align by hand.
- Comments and commit messages in English only.
- A comment describes the behaviour that exists, not the intended one. Change the behaviour, fix the comment in the
  same commit.
- Epic prefixes: `b` for bool, `F/U/A/E/I` for types.

## Decomposition

- A decision (who is hit, how much damage, what a rule allows, when the run ends) lives in a pure
  `namespace <Feature>Rules` with no world and no actors: `Public/<System>/<Feature>Rules.h`, free functions with
  `JAMGAME_API`, and a header line `Tests: Jam.<Area>.*`.
- An actor, component or subsystem only glues: collects inputs, calls the rule, applies the result.
- A big class is split into `.cpp` files by responsibility with one shared `.h`.
- Soft thresholds: a `.cpp` over ~600 lines, a function over ~60, nesting over 3. Exceeding one is a signal, not a
  ban: split or justify.

## Systems and dependencies

- Folders `Public/<System>` and `Private/<System>`, plus `Tests`.
- **The simulation does not know about the presentation.** `Core` and `Sim` never include `View`, `UI` or `Audio`.
  The directions are forbidden in the `check_code.py` ratchet (`SIMULATION`, `PRESENTATION`): extend both lists when
  a new system folder appears.
- Balance numbers (prices, health, damage, timings) live in data, not in code.
- Randomness of the simulation comes from a seeded stream, not `FMath::Rand`, so a run can be replayed in a test.

## Logs

- No `LogTemp` in new code. Use the category of the system or `DEFINE_LOG_CATEGORY_STATIC` for a single file.
- Warning and Error only for a breakage or a wrong setup; state changes are `Verbose`, per-tick traces `VeryVerbose`.

## Tests

- Every new decision in `*Rules` gets a test `Jam.<Area>.<Case>` before the code (test first). Glue with the engine
  is checked in PIE, a test is optional.
- The number of `Jam.` tests only grows; a failing test means reverting the change, not bending the test to the code.
- A bug is fixed separately from a refactoring, test first.

## Blueprint seam

"""Per clip of a GLB: duration and the hips' travel (first to last key, and the widest swing), in the file's units."""
import json
import struct
import sys

data = open(sys.argv[1], "rb").read()
jlen = struct.unpack_from("<I", data, 12)[0]
doc = json.loads(data[20:20 + jlen])
blen_at = 20 + jlen
binary = data[blen_at + 8:]
SIZES = {"SCALAR": 1, "VEC3": 3, "VEC4": 4}


def read(index):
    acc = doc["accessors"][index]
    view = doc["bufferViews"][acc["bufferView"]]
    n = SIZES[acc["type"]]
    start = view.get("byteOffset", 0) + acc.get("byteOffset", 0)
    flat = struct.unpack_from("<%df" % (acc["count"] * n), binary, start)
    return [flat[i * n:(i + 1) * n] for i in range(acc["count"])]


names = {i: n.get("name") for i, n in enumerate(doc["nodes"])}
hips = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "pelvis"
for anim in doc.get("animations", []):
    for ch in anim["channels"]:
        if names[ch["target"]["node"]] != hips or ch["target"]["path"] != "translation":
            continue
        sampler = anim["samplers"][ch["sampler"]]
        times = read(sampler["input"])
        pos = read(sampler["output"])
        first, last = pos[0], pos[-1]
        swing = max(((p[0] - first[0]) ** 2 + (p[2] - first[2]) ** 2) ** 0.5 for p in pos)
        print("%-24s %5.2f s  start %s  end-start %s  widest %.3f  height %.3f..%.3f" % (
            anim.get("name"), times[-1][0], tuple(round(v, 3) for v in first),
            tuple(round(b - a, 3) for a, b in zip(first, last)), swing,
            min(p[1] for p in pos), max(p[1] for p in pos)))

"""Imports the approved 3D models into the project. Runs inside the editor, headless:

UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe JamGame.uproject -run=pythonscript -script="Tools/Editor/import_models.py"

The hero (Meshy model, rig and clips), the Publisher (our rebuilt rig, Art/Models/boss_fixed) and the props. FBX
goes through the classic importer (its options are stable from a script), GLB through Interchange. An asset that
exists is imported again over itself, so the script can be run after every new export. The report of what arrived
(bones, height, clips) goes to the log under "import_models:".
"""
import os

import unreal

ROOT = unreal.Paths.convert_relative_path_to_full(unreal.Paths.project_dir())
ART = os.path.join(ROOT, "Art")
HERO = "/Game/Characters/Hero"
BOSS = "/Game/Characters/Publisher"
PROPS = "/Game/Props"

HERO_MESH = ("Models/hero_rig/result.rigged_character_fbx_url.fbx", "SK_Hero")
HERO_CLIPS = [
    ("Models/hero_clips/result.animation_fbx_url.fbx", None),
    ("Models/hero_rig/result.basic_animations.walking_fbx_url.fbx", "A_Hero_Walk"),
    ("Models/hero_rig/result.basic_animations.running_fbx_url.fbx", "A_Hero_Run"),
]
BOSS_MESH = ("Models/boss_fixed/SK_Publisher.fbx", "SK_Publisher")
BOSS_CLIPS = ["Idle", "Slow_Orc_Walk", "Heavy_Hammer_Swing", "Charged_Ground_Slam", "Kung_Fu_Punch", "Hit_Reaction",
              "Knock_Down", "T_Pose"]
# The clips that carry travel on root (boss_fixed/README.md): the game keeps him in place.
BOSS_ROOT_LOCKED = ["Hit_Reaction", "Knock_Down", "Kung_Fu_Punch"]
PROP_MODELS = [
    ("Models/katana/model_glb.glb", "SM_Katana"),
    ("Models/shuriken/model_glb.glb", "SM_Shuriken"),
    ("Models/cash_stack/model_glb.glb", "SM_CashStack"),
]
PROP_TEXTURES = [
    ("Concepts/r5_dollar_card.png", "T_DollarCard"),
    ("Concepts/r5_memo_card.png", "T_MemoCard"),
]


def log(text):
    unreal.log("import_models: " + text)


def run(task):
    unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().import_asset_tasks([task])
    return list(task.get_editor_property("imported_object_paths"))


def task_for(source, folder, name, options=None):
    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()
    task.set_editor_property("filename", os.path.join(ART, source))
    task.set_editor_property("destination_path", folder)
    if name:
        task.set_editor_property("destination_name", name)
    task.set_editor_property("automated", True)
    task.set_editor_property("replace_existing", True)
    task.set_editor_property("save", True)
    if options:
        task.set_editor_property("options", options)
    return task


def fbx_options(skeleton=None):
    ui = unreal.FbxImportUI()
    ui.set_editor_property("automated_import_should_detect_type", False)
    ui.set_editor_property("mesh_type_to_import", unreal.FBXImportType.FBXIT_ANIMATION if skeleton else unreal.FBXImportType.FBXIT_SKELETAL_MESH)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_mesh", skeleton is None)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_as_skeletal", True)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_animations", skeleton is not None)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_materials", skeleton is None)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_textures", skeleton is None)
    ui.set_editor_property("create_physics_asset", False)
    if skeleton:
        ui.set_editor_property("skeleton", skeleton)
        anim = ui.get_editor_property("anim_sequence_import_data")
        anim.set_editor_property("animation_length", unreal.FBXAnimationLengthImportType.FBXALIT_EXPORTED_TIME)
        anim.set_editor_property("import_bone_tracks", True)
        anim.set_editor_property("remove_redundant_keys", False)
    mesh = ui.get_editor_property("skeletal_mesh_import_data")
    mesh.set_editor_property("normal_import_method", unreal.FBXNormalImportMethod.FBXNIM_IMPORT_NORMALS)
    return ui


def report_mesh(path):
    mesh = unreal.load_asset(path)
    if not mesh:
        log("MISSING " + path)
        return None
    skeleton = mesh.get_editor_property("skeleton")
    box = mesh.get_bounds().box_extent
    origin = mesh.get_bounds().origin
    bones = [str(n) for n in skeleton.get_editor_property("bone_tree")] if False else []
    log("%s: skeleton %s, bounds origin %s extent %s" % (path, skeleton.get_path_name(), origin, box))
    return skeleton


def import_character(mesh_source, folder, clips, locked):
    source, name = mesh_source
    paths = run(task_for(source, folder, name, fbx_options()))
    log("mesh %s -> %s" % (source, paths))
    skeleton = report_mesh("%s/%s" % (folder, name))
    if not skeleton:
        return
    for clip_source, clip_name in clips:
        paths = run(task_for(clip_source, folder + "/Anims", clip_name, fbx_options(skeleton)))
        for path in paths:
            seq = unreal.load_asset(path)
            if not isinstance(seq, unreal.AnimSequence):
                continue
            short = path.split(".")[-1]
            if any(short.endswith(k) for k in locked):
                seq.set_editor_property("force_root_lock", True)
                seq.set_editor_property("root_motion_root_lock", unreal.RootMotionRootLock.REF_POSE)
                unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(seq, False)
            log("clip %s: %.2f s, root lock %s" % (path, seq.get_play_length(), seq.get_editor_property("force_root_lock")))


def import_props():
    for source, name in PROP_MODELS:
        log("prop %s -> %s" % (source, run(task_for(source, PROPS, name))))
    for source, name in PROP_TEXTURES:
        log("texture %s -> %s" % (source, run(task_for(source, PROPS + "/Textures", name))))


unreal.SystemLibrary.execute_console_command(None, "Interchange.FeatureFlags.Import.FBX 0")
import_character(HERO_MESH, HERO, HERO_CLIPS, [])
import_character(BOSS_MESH, BOSS, [("Models/boss_fixed/%s.fbx" % c, "A_Publisher_" + c) for c in BOSS_CLIPS], BOSS_ROOT_LOCKED)
import_props()
log("done")

BOSS_MESH = ("Models/boss_fixed/SK_Publisher.fbx", "SK_Publisher")
BOSS_CLIPS = ["Idle", "Slow_Orc_Walk", "Heavy_Hammer_Swing", "Charged_Ground_Slam", "Kung_Fu_Punch", "Hit_Reaction",
              "Knock_Down", "T_Pose"]
# The clips that carry travel on root (boss_fixed/README.md): the game keeps him in place.
BOSS_ROOT_LOCKED = ["Hit_Reaction", "Knock_Down", "Kung_Fu_Punch"]
PROP_MODELS = [
    ("Models/katana/model_glb.glb", "SM_Katana"),
    ("Models/shuriken/model_glb.glb", "SM_Shuriken"),
    ("Models/cash_stack/model_glb.glb", "SM_CashStack"),
]
PROP_TEXTURES = [
    ("Concepts/r5_dollar_card.png", "T_DollarCard"),
    ("Concepts/r5_memo_card.png", "T_MemoCard"),
]


def log(text):
    unreal.log("import_models: " + text)


def run(task):
    unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().import_asset_tasks([task])
    return list(task.get_editor_property("imported_object_paths"))


def task_for(source, folder, name, options=None):
    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()
    task.set_editor_property("filename", os.path.join(ART, source))
    task.set_editor_property("destination_path", folder)
    if name:
        task.set_editor_property("destination_name", name)
    task.set_editor_property("automated", True)
    task.set_editor_property("replace_existing", True)
    task.set_editor_property("save", True)
    if options:
        task.set_editor_property("options", options)
    return task


def fbx_options(skeleton=None):
    ui = unreal.FbxImportUI()
    ui.set_editor_property("automated_import_should_detect_type", False)
    ui.set_editor_property("mesh_type_to_import", unreal.FBXImportType.FBXIT_ANIMATION if skeleton else unreal.FBXImportType.FBXIT_SKELETAL_MESH)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_mesh", skeleton is None)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_as_skeletal", True)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_animations", skeleton is not None)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_materials", skeleton is None)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_textures", skeleton is None)
    ui.set_editor_property("create_physics_asset", False)
    if skeleton:
        ui.set_editor_property("skeleton", skeleton)
        anim = ui.get_editor_property("anim_sequence_import_data")
        anim.set_editor_property("animation_length", unreal.FBXAnimationLengthImportType.FBXALIT_EXPORTED_TIME)
        anim.set_editor_property("import_bone_tracks", True)
        anim.set_editor_property("remove_redundant_keys", False)
    mesh = ui.get_editor_property("skeletal_mesh_import_data")
    mesh.set_editor_property("normal_import_method", unreal.FBXNormalImportMethod.FBXNIM_IMPORT_NORMALS)
    return ui


def report_mesh(path):
    mesh = unreal.load_asset(path)
    if not mesh:
        log("MISSING " + path)
        return None
    skeleton = mesh.get_editor_property("skeleton")
    box = mesh.get_bounds().box_extent
    origin = mesh.get_bounds().origin
    bones = [str(n) for n in skeleton.get_editor_property("bone_tree")] if False else []
    log("%s: skeleton %s, bounds origin %s extent %s" % (path, skeleton.get_path_name(), origin, box))
    return skeleton


def import_character(mesh_source, folder, clips, locked):
    source, name = mesh_source
    paths = run(task_for(source, folder, name, fbx_options()))
    log("mesh %s -> %s" % (source, paths))
    skeleton = report_mesh("%s/%s" % (folder, name))
    if not skeleton:
        return
    for clip_source, clip_name in clips:
        paths = run(task_for(clip_source, folder + "/Anims", clip_name, fbx_options(skeleton)))
        for path in paths:
            seq = unreal.load_asset(path)
            if not isinstance(seq, unreal.AnimSequence):
                continue
            short = path.split(".")[-1]
            if any(short.endswith(k) for k in locked):
                seq.set_editor_property("force_root_lock", True)
                seq.set_editor_property("root_motion_root_lock", unreal.RootMotionRootLock.REF_POSE)
                unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(seq, False)
            log("clip %s: %.2f s, root lock %s" % (path, seq.get_play_length(), seq.get_editor_property("force_root_lock")))


def import_props():
    for source, name in PROP_MODELS:
        log("prop %s -> %s" % (source, run(task_for(source, PROPS, name))))
    for source, name in PROP_TEXTURES:
        log("texture %s -> %s" % (source, run(task_for(source, PROPS + "/Textures", name))))


unreal.SystemLibrary.execute_console_command(None, "Interchange.FeatureFlags.Import.FBX 0")
import_character(HERO_MESH, HERO, HERO_CLIPS, [])
import_character(BOSS_MESH, BOSS, [("Models/boss_fixed/%s.fbx" % c, "A_Publisher_" + c) for c in BOSS_CLIPS], BOSS_ROOT_LOCKED)
import_props()
log("done")

"""
KIND: offline tool (headless Blender, writes the FBX files of Art/Models/boss_fixed).

Exports the reworked Publisher for Unreal: SK_Publisher.fbx (mesh, skeleton, embedded textures, no animation) and one
armature-only FBX per clip, named as the clip. The data is converted to centimetres first (rest bones, mesh and
location keys times 100, scene unit 0.01), so the file has unit scale 1 and no scaled armature node: root motion
comes into Unreal in true size whatever the importer does with units.

    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/publisher_rig/export_fbx.py -- <clips.blend> <out_dir> [probe.json]

probe.json receives world positions (cm) of every bone at a few frames of every clip, for verify_fbx.py.
"""
import json
import os
import sys

import bpy

SCALE = 100.0
MESH_FILE = "SK_Publisher.fbx"


def fcurves(action):
    for layer in action.layers:
        for strip in layer.strips:
            for bag in strip.channelbags:
                yield from bag.fcurves


def to_centimetres(scene, arm, mesh):
    scene.unit_settings.system = "METRIC"
    scene.unit_settings.scale_length = 1.0 / SCALE
    arm.animation_data.action = None
    for pb in arm.pose.bones:
        pb.matrix_basis.identity()
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action="DESELECT")
    # The mesh is a child of the armature and takes its scale from it.
    assert mesh.parent == arm
    height = mesh.dimensions.z
    arm.scale = (SCALE, SCALE, SCALE)
    for ob in (arm, mesh):
        ob.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = arm
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=False, rotation=False, scale=True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.update()
    assert abs(mesh.dimensions.z - height * SCALE) < 0.01 * height * SCALE, mesh.dimensions.z
    assert all(abs(s - 1) < 1e-6 for ob in (arm, mesh) for s in ob.matrix_world.to_scale())
    for action in bpy.data.actions:
        for fc in fcurves(action):
            if fc.data_path.endswith(".location"):
                for key in fc.keyframe_points:
                    key.co[1] *= SCALE
                    key.handle_left[1] *= SCALE
                    key.handle_right[1] *= SCALE
                fc.update()


def export(path, objects, animated):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action="DESELECT")
    for ob in objects:
        ob.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = objects[0]
    bpy.ops.export_scene.fbx(
        filepath=path, use_selection=True, object_types={"ARMATURE", "MESH"}, global_scale=1.0,
        apply_unit_scale=True, apply_scale_options="FBX_SCALE_NONE", axis_forward="-Z", axis_up="Y",
        add_leaf_bones=False, primary_bone_axis="Y", secondary_bone_axis="X", use_armature_deform_only=False,
        armature_nodetype="NULL", mesh_smooth_type="FACE", use_tspace=False, use_mesh_modifiers=True,

scene = bpy.context.scene
    scene.render.fps = FPS
    for ob in list(bpy.data.objects):
        bpy.data.objects.remove(ob)
    objects = import_glb(CLIPS_GLB)
    arm = next(o for o in objects if o.type == "ARMATURE")
    mesh = next(o for o in objects if o.type == "MESH")
    for name, path in EXTRA.items():
        known = set(bpy.data.actions)
        extra = import_glb(path)
        new = [a for a in bpy.data.actions if a not in known]
        assert len(new) == 1, [a.name for a in new]
        new[0].name = name
        for ob in extra:
            bpy.data.objects.remove(ob)
    for action in bpy.data.actions:
        action.use_fake_user = True
    print("[hero] actions: %s" % sorted(a.name for a in bpy.data.actions))
    add_root(arm)
    for name in TRAVEL:
        move_travel(scene, arm, bpy.data.actions[name])
    arm.name = "Armature"
    mesh.name = "SK_Hero"
    if mesh.parent != arm:
        mesh.parent = arm
    print("[hero] arm %s mesh %s parent %s dims %s" % (tuple(arm.matrix_world.to_scale()), tuple(mesh.matrix_world.to_scale()), mesh.parent, tuple(mesh.dimensions)))
    print("[hero] arm rot %s mesh local %s" % (tuple(arm.matrix_world.to_euler()), mesh.matrix_parent_inverse))
    to_centimetres(scene, arm, mesh)
    export(os.path.join(out_dir, "SK_Hero.fbx"), [arm, mesh], False)
    print("[hero] SK_Hero.fbx: %d bones, %d verts, %.1f cm tall" % (len(arm.data.bones), len(mesh.data.vertices), mesh.dimensions.z))
    for action in sorted(bpy.data.actions, key=lambda a: a.name):
        arm.animation_data.action = action
        arm.animation_data.action_slot = action.slots[0]
        first, last = (int(round(f)) for f in action.frame_range)
        scene.frame_start, scene.frame_end = first, last
        export(os.path.join(out_dir, action.name + ".fbx"), [arm], True)
        print("[hero] %s.fbx: frames %d..%d" % (action.name, first, last))


main()

"""
KIND: offline tool (headless Blender, writes the FBX files of Art/Models/hero_fixed).

Exports the Meshy hero for Unreal the way the Publisher is exported (Tools/Art/publisher_rig/export_fbx.py):
SK_Hero.fbx (mesh, skeleton, embedded textures, no animation) and one armature-only FBX per clip, in centimetres.

Two changes to the Meshy data on the way:
- a `root` bone at the origin on the ground becomes the parent of `pelvis` (Meshy rigs have none);
- in the clips that travel (TRAVEL) the horizontal travel of the hips moves from `pelvis` to `root`, so Unreal's
  Force Root Lock keeps him in place while the hips still drop and sway.

    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/hero_export.py -- <out_dir>
"""
import os
import sys

import bpy
from mathutils import Matrix, Vector

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(HERE, "publisher_rig"))
from export_fbx import export, to_centimetres  # noqa: E402

ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", ".."))
MODELS = os.path.join(ROOT, "Art", "Models")
CLIPS_GLB = os.path.join(MODELS, "hero_clips", "result.animation_glb_url.glb")
EXTRA = {
    "Walk": os.path.join(MODELS, "hero_rig", "result.basic_animations.walking_armature_glb_url.glb"),
    "Run": os.path.join(MODELS, "hero_rig", "result.basic_animations.running_armature_glb_url.glb"),
}
TRAVEL = ["Hit_Reaction", "Dead", "Roll_Dodge"]
FPS = 30


def import_glb(path):
    before = set(bpy.data.objects)
    bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=path)
    return [o for o in bpy.data.objects if o not in before]


def add_root(arm):
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = arm
    bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode="EDIT")
    bones = arm.data.edit_bones
    root = bones.new("root")
    root.head = Vector((0, 0, 0))
    root.tail = Vector((0, 0.2, 0))
    bones["pelvis"].parent = root
    bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode="OBJECT")


def move_travel(scene, arm, action):
    """Keys root with the horizontal travel of pelvis from the first frame, and pelvis without it."""
    arm.animation_data.action = action
    arm.animation_data.action_slot = action.slots[0]
    first, last = (int(round(f)) for f in action.frame_range)
    root, pelvis = arm.pose.bones["root"], arm.pose.bones["pelvis"]
    scene.frame_set(first)
    start = pelvis.matrix.translation.copy()
    frames = {}
    for frame in range(first, last + 1):
        scene.frame_set(frame)
        frames[frame] = pelvis.matrix.copy()
    for frame, hips in frames.items():
        travel = hips.translation - start
        travel.z = 0.0
        root.matrix = Matrix.Translation(travel)
        bpy.context.view_layer.update()
        pelvis.matrix = hips
        bpy.context.view_layer.update()
        root.keyframe_insert("location", frame=frame)
        pelvis.keyframe_insert("location", frame=frame)
        pelvis.keyframe_insert("rotation_quaternion", frame=frame)
    print("[hero] %s: travel %.3f m moved to root" % (action.name, (frames[last].translation - start).to_2d().length))


def main():
    out_dir = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1]
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    scene = bpy.context.scene
    scene.render.fps = FPS
    for ob in list(bpy.data.objects):
        bpy.data.objects.remove(ob)
    objects = import_glb(CLIPS_GLB)
    arm = next(o for o in objects if o.type == "ARMATURE")
    mesh = next(o for o in objects if o.type == "MESH")
    for name, path in EXTRA.items():
        known = set(bpy.data.actions)
        extra = import_glb(path)
        new = [a for a in bpy.data.actions if a not in known]
        assert len(new) == 1, [a.name for a in new]
        new[0].name = name
        for ob in extra:
            bpy.data.objects.remove(ob)
    for action in bpy.data.actions:
        action.use_fake_user = True
    print("[hero] actions: %s" % sorted(a.name for a in bpy.data.actions))
    add_root(arm)
    for name in TRAVEL:
        move_travel(scene, arm, bpy.data.actions[name])
    arm.name = "Armature"
    mesh.name = "SK_Hero"
    if mesh.parent != arm:
        mesh.parent = arm
    print("[hero] arm %s mesh %s parent %s dims %s" % (tuple(arm.matrix_world.to_scale()), tuple(mesh.matrix_world.to_scale()), mesh.parent, tuple(mesh.dimensions)))
    print("[hero] arm rot %s mesh local %s" % (tuple(arm.matrix_world.to_euler()), mesh.matrix_parent_inverse))
    to_centimetres(scene, arm, mesh)
    export(os.path.join(out_dir, "SK_Hero.fbx"), [arm, mesh], False)
    print("[hero] SK_Hero.fbx: %d bones, %d verts, %.1f cm tall" % (len(arm.data.bones), len(mesh.data.vertices), mesh.dimensions.z))
    for action in sorted(bpy.data.actions, key=lambda a: a.name):
        arm.animation_data.action = action
        arm.animation_data.action_slot = action.slots[0]
        first, last = (int(round(f)) for f in action.frame_range)
        scene.frame_start, scene.frame_end = first, last
        export(os.path.join(out_dir, action.name + ".fbx"), [arm], True)
        print("[hero] %s.fbx: frames %d..%d" % (action.name, first, last))


main()

"""
KIND: offline tool (headless Blender, writes the FBX files of Art/Models/hero_fixed).

Exports the Meshy hero for Unreal the way the Publisher is exported (Tools/Art/publisher_rig/export_fbx.py):
SK_Hero.fbx (mesh, skeleton, embedded textures, no animation) and one armature-only FBX per clip, in centimetres.

Two changes to the Meshy data on the way:
- a `root` bone at the origin on the ground becomes the parent of `pelvis` (Meshy rigs have none);
- in the clips that travel (TRAVEL) the horizontal travel of the hips moves from `pelvis` to `root`, so Unreal's
  Force Root Lock keeps him in place while the hips still drop and sway.

    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/hero_export.py -- <out_dir>
"""
import os
import sys

import bpy
from mathutils import Matrix, Vector

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(HERE, "publisher_rig"))
from export_fbx import export, to_centimetres  # noqa: E402

ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", ".."))
MODELS = os.path.join(ROOT, "Art", "Models")
CLIPS_GLB = os.path.join(MODELS, "hero_clips", "result.animation_glb_url.glb")
EXTRA = {
    "Walk": os.path.join(MODELS, "hero_rig", "result.basic_animations.walking_armature_glb_url.glb"),
    "Run": os.path.join(MODELS, "hero_rig", "result.basic_animations.running_armature_glb_url.glb"),
}
TRAVEL = ["Hit_Reaction", "Dead", "Roll_Dodge"]
FPS = 30


def import_glb(path):
    before = set(bpy.data.objects)
    bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=path)
    return [o for o in bpy.data.objects if o not in before]


def add_root(arm):
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = arm
    bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode="EDIT")
    bones = arm.data.edit_bones
    root = bones.new("root")
    root.head = Vector((0, 0, 0))
    root.tail = Vector((0, 0.2, 0))
    bones["pelvis"].parent = root
    bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode="OBJECT")


def move_travel(scene, arm, action):
    """Keys root with the horizontal travel of pelvis from the first frame, and pelvis without it."""
    arm.animation_data.action = action
    arm.animation_data.action_slot = action.slots[0]
    first, last = (int(round(f)) for f in action.frame_range)
    root, pelvis = arm.pose.bones["root"], arm.pose.bones["pelvis"]
    scene.frame_set(first)
    start = pelvis.matrix.translation.copy()
    frames = {}
    for frame in range(first, last + 1):
        scene.frame_set(frame)
        frames[frame] = pelvis.matrix.copy()
    for frame, hips in frames.items():
        travel = hips.translation - start
        travel.z = 0.0
        root.matrix = Matrix.Translation(travel)
        bpy.context.view_layer.update()
        pelvis.matrix = hips
        bpy.context.view_layer.update()
        root.keyframe_insert("location", frame=frame)
        pelvis.keyframe_insert("location", frame=frame)
        pelvis.keyframe_insert("rotation_quaternion", frame=frame)
    print("[hero] %s: travel %.3f m moved to root" % (action.name, (frames[last].translation - start).to_2d().length))


def main():
    out_dir = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1]
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    scene = bpy.context.scene
    scene.render.fps = FPS
    for ob in list(bpy.data.objects):
        bpy.data.objects.remove(ob)
    objects = import_glb(CLIPS_GLB)
    arm = next(o for o in objects if o.type == "ARMATURE")
    mesh = next(o for o in objects if o.type == "MESH")
    for name, path in EXTRA.items():
        known = set(bpy.data.actions)
        extra = import_glb(path)
        new = [a for a in bpy.data.actions if a not in known]
        assert len(new) == 1, [a.name for a in new]
        new[0].name = name
        for ob in extra:
            bpy.data.objects.remove(ob)
    for action in bpy.data.actions:
        action.use_fake_user = True
    print("[hero] actions: %s" % sorted(a.name for a in bpy.data.actions))
    assert mesh.parent == arm
    # The glTF armature is turned 90 degrees (Y up): made the rest pose, armature space becomes Z-up world space.
    arm.animation_data.action = None
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action="DESELECT")
    for ob in (arm, mesh):
        ob.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = arm
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=True, rotation=True, scale=True)
    add_root(arm)
    for name in TRAVEL:
        move_travel(scene, arm, bpy.data.actions[name])
    arm.name = "Armature"
    mesh.name = "SK_Hero"
    arm.animation_data.action = None
    for pb in arm.pose.bones:
        pb.matrix_basis.identity()
    bpy.context.view_layer.update()
    zs = [(mesh.matrix_world @ v.co).z for v in mesh.data.vertices]
    print("[hero] rest pose: feet %.3f m, top %.3f m" % (min(zs), max(zs)))
    to_centimetres(scene, arm, mesh)
    export(os.path.join(out_dir, "SK_Hero.fbx"), [arm, mesh], False)
    print("[hero] SK_Hero.fbx: %d bones, %d verts, %.1f cm tall" % (len(arm.data.bones), len(mesh.data.vertices), mesh.dimensions.z))
    for action in sorted(bpy.data.actions, key=lambda a: a.name):
        arm.animation_data.action = action
        arm.animation_data.action_slot = action.slots[0]
        first, last = (int(round(f)) for f in action.frame_range)
        scene.frame_start, scene.frame_end = first, last
        export(os.path.join(out_dir, action.name + ".fbx"), [arm], True)
        print("[hero] %s.fbx: frames %d..%d" % (action.name, first, last))


main()

"""Imports the approved 3D models into the project. Runs inside the editor, headless:

UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe JamGame.uproject -run=pythonscript -script="Tools/Editor/import_models.py"

The hero (Art/Models/hero_fixed, exported by Tools/Art/hero_export.py), the Publisher (Art/Models/boss_fixed) and the
props. Both characters come as one mesh FBX in centimetres plus one FBX per clip; FBX goes through the classic
importer (its options are stable from a script), GLB through Interchange. An asset that exists is imported again
over itself, so the script can be run after every new export.
"""
import os

import unreal

ROOT = unreal.Paths.convert_relative_path_to_full(unreal.Paths.project_dir())
ART = os.path.join(ROOT, "Art")

CHARACTERS = [
    {
        "folder": "/Game/Characters/Hero",
        "source": "Models/hero_fixed",
        "mesh": "SK_Hero",
        "prefix": "A_Hero_",
        "clips": ["Idle", "Walk", "Run", "Right_Hand_Sword_Slash", "Left_Slash", "Sword_Parry", "Hit_Reaction", "Dead",
                  "Roll_Dodge"],
        # Clips whose travel is on root (hero_export.py, boss_fixed/README.md): the game keeps the fighter in place.
        "locked": ["Hit_Reaction", "Dead", "Roll_Dodge"],
    },
    {
        "folder": "/Game/Characters/Publisher",
        "source": "Models/boss_fixed",
        "mesh": "SK_Publisher",
        "prefix": "A_Publisher_",
        "clips": ["Idle", "Slow_Orc_Walk", "Heavy_Hammer_Swing", "Charged_Ground_Slam", "Kung_Fu_Punch", "Hit_Reaction",
                  "Knock_Down", "T_Pose"],
        "locked": ["Hit_Reaction", "Knock_Down", "Kung_Fu_Punch"],
    },
]
PROP_MODELS = [
    ("Models/katana/model_glb.glb", "Katana", "SM_Katana"),
    ("Models/shuriken/model_glb.glb", "Shuriken", "SM_Shuriken"),
    ("Models/cash_stack/model_glb.glb", "CashStack", "SM_CashStack"),
]
PROP_TEXTURES = [
    ("Concepts/r5_dollar_card.png", "T_DollarCard"),
    ("Concepts/r5_memo_card.png", "T_MemoCard"),
]


def log(text):
    unreal.log("import_models: " + text)


def run(task):
    unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().import_asset_tasks([task])
    return list(task.get_editor_property("imported_object_paths"))


def task_for(source, folder, name, options=None):
    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()
    task.set_editor_property("filename", os.path.join(ART, source))
    task.set_editor_property("destination_path", folder)
    task.set_editor_property("destination_name", name)
    task.set_editor_property("automated", True)
    task.set_editor_property("replace_existing", True)
    task.set_editor_property("save", True)
    if options:
        task.set_editor_property("options", options)
    return task


def fbx_options(skeleton=None):
    ui = unreal.FbxImportUI()
    ui.set_editor_property("automated_import_should_detect_type", False)
    ui.set_editor_property("mesh_type_to_import", unreal.FBXImportType.FBXIT_ANIMATION if skeleton else unreal.FBXImportType.FBXIT_SKELETAL_MESH)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_mesh", skeleton is None)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_as_skeletal", True)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_animations", skeleton is not None)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_materials", skeleton is None)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_textures", skeleton is None)
    ui.set_editor_property("create_physics_asset", False)
    if skeleton:
        ui.set_editor_property("skeleton", skeleton)
        anim = ui.get_editor_property("anim_sequence_import_data")
        anim.set_editor_property("animation_length", unreal.FBXAnimationLengthImportType.FBXALIT_EXPORTED_TIME)

"""Imports the approved 3D models into the project. Runs inside the editor, headless:

UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe JamGame.uproject -run=pythonscript -script="Tools/Editor/import_models.py"

The hero (Meshy model, rig and clips), the Publisher (our rebuilt rig, Art/Models/boss_fixed) and the props. FBX
goes through the classic importer (its options are stable from a script), GLB through Interchange. An asset that
exists is imported again over itself, so the script can be run after every new export. The report of what arrived
(bones, height, clips) goes to the log under "import_models:".
"""
import os

import unreal

ROOT = unreal.Paths.convert_relative_path_to_full(unreal.Paths.project_dir())
ART = os.path.join(ROOT, "Art")
HERO = "/Game/Characters/Hero"
BOSS = "/Game/Characters/Publisher"
PROPS = "/Game/Props"

HERO_MESH = ("Models/hero_rig/result.rigged_character_fbx_url.fbx", "SK_Hero")
HERO_CLIPS = [
    ("Models/hero_clips/result.animation_fbx_url.fbx", None),
    ("Models/hero_rig/result.basic_animations.walking_fbx_url.fbx", "A_Hero_Walk"),
    ("Models/hero_rig/result.basic_animations.running_fbx_url.fbx", "A_Hero_Run"),
]
BOSS_MESH = ("Models/boss_fixed/SK_Publisher.fbx", "SK_Publisher")
BOSS_CLIPS = ["Idle", "Slow_Orc_Walk", "Heavy_Hammer_Swing", "Charged_Ground_Slam", "Kung_Fu_Punch", "Hit_Reaction",
              "Knock_Down", "T_Pose"]
# The clips that carry travel on root (boss_fixed/README.md): the game keeps him in place.
BOSS_ROOT_LOCKED = ["Hit_Reaction", "Knock_Down", "Kung_Fu_Punch"]
PROP_MODELS = [
    ("Models/katana/model_glb.glb", "SM_Katana"),
    ("Models/shuriken/model_glb.glb", "SM_Shuriken"),
    ("Models/cash_stack/model_glb.glb", "SM_CashStack"),
]
PROP_TEXTURES = [
    ("Concepts/r5_dollar_card.png", "T_DollarCard"),
    ("Concepts/r5_memo_card.png", "T_MemoCard"),
]


def log(text):
    unreal.log("import_models: " + text)


def run(task):
    unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().import_asset_tasks([task])
    return list(task.get_editor_property("imported_object_paths"))


def task_for(source, folder, name, options=None):
    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()
    task.set_editor_property("filename", os.path.join(ART, source))
    task.set_editor_property("destination_path", folder)
    if name:
        task.set_editor_property("destination_name", name)
    task.set_editor_property("automated", True)
    task.set_editor_property("replace_existing", True)
    task.set_editor_property("save", True)
    if options:
        task.set_editor_property("options", options)
    return task


def fbx_options(skeleton=None):
    ui = unreal.FbxImportUI()
    ui.set_editor_property("automated_import_should_detect_type", False)
    ui.set_editor_property("mesh_type_to_import", unreal.FBXImportType.FBXIT_ANIMATION if skeleton else unreal.FBXImportType.FBXIT_SKELETAL_MESH)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_mesh", skeleton is None)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_as_skeletal", True)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_animations", skeleton is not None)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_materials", skeleton is None)
    ui.set_editor_property("import_textures", skeleton is None)
    ui.set_editor_property("create_physics_asset", False)
    if skeleton:
        ui.set_editor_property("skeleton", skeleton)
        anim = ui.get_editor_property("anim_sequence_import_data")
        anim.set_editor_property("animation_length", unreal.FBXAnimationLengthImportType.FBXALIT_EXPORTED_TIME)
        anim.set_editor_property("import_bone_tracks", True)
        anim.set_editor_property("remove_redundant_keys", False)
    mesh = ui.get_editor_property("skeletal_mesh_import_data")
    mesh.set_editor_property("normal_import_method", unreal.FBXNormalImportMethod.FBXNIM_IMPORT_NORMALS)
    return ui


def report_mesh(path):
    mesh = unreal.load_asset(path)
    if not mesh:
        log("MISSING " + path)
        return None
    skeleton = mesh.get_editor_property("skeleton")
    box = mesh.get_bounds().box_extent
    origin = mesh.get_bounds().origin
    log("%s: skeleton %s, bounds origin %s extent %s" % (path, skeleton.get_path_name(), origin, box))
    return skeleton


def import_character(mesh_source, folder, clips, locked):
    source, name = mesh_source
    paths = run(task_for(source, folder, name, fbx_options()))
    log("mesh %s -> %s" % (source, paths))
    skeleton = report_mesh("%s/%s" % (folder, name))
    if not skeleton:
        return
    for clip_source, clip_name in clips:
        paths = run(task_for(clip_source, folder + "/Anims", clip_name, fbx_options(skeleton)))
        for path in paths:
            seq = unreal.load_asset(path)
            if not isinstance(seq, unreal.AnimSequence):
                continue
            short = path.split(".")[-1]
            if any(short.endswith(k) for k in locked):
                seq.set_editor_property("force_root_lock", True)
                seq.set_editor_property("root_motion_root_lock", unreal.RootMotionRootLock.REF_POSE)
                unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(seq, False)
            log("clip %s: %.2f s, root lock %s" % (path, seq.get_play_length(), seq.get_editor_property("force_root_lock")))


def import_props():
    for source, name in PROP_MODELS:
        log("prop %s -> %s" % (source, run(task_for(source, PROPS, name))))
    for source, name in PROP_TEXTURES:
        log("texture %s -> %s" % (source, run(task_for(source, PROPS + "/Textures", name))))


unreal.SystemLibrary.execute_console_command(None, "Interchange.FeatureFlags.Import.FBX 0")
import_character(HERO_MESH, HERO, HERO_CLIPS, [])
import_character(BOSS_MESH, BOSS, [("Models/boss_fixed/%s.fbx" % c, "A_Publisher_" + c) for c in BOSS_CLIPS], BOSS_ROOT_LOCKED)
import_props()
log("done")

"""Creates the material of the 3D characters and puts it on them. Runs inside the editor, headless, after
import_models.py:

UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe JamGame.uproject -run=pythonscript -script="Tools/Editor/create_character_materials.py"

M_JamCharacter is the PBR look of the Meshy textures plus two things the game drives:
- Flash (0 to 1) turns the body white and bright for a hit, FlashColor times FlashGlow in emission;
- the neon: the saturated parts of the base colour (the hero's cyan and magenta piping) shine NeonGlow times.
Metallic and roughness come from any channel of their textures (the hero has them packed in one glTF image, the
Publisher in two grey ones): MetallicChannel and RoughnessChannel pick it.
The textures come from Art/Models/<x>_fixed/textures (Tools/Art/save_textures.py). Running it again rebuilds the
material and the instances.
"""
import os

import unreal

ROOT = unreal.Paths.convert_relative_path_to_full(unreal.Paths.project_dir())
FOLDER = "/Game/Characters/Materials"
MASTER = "M_JamCharacter"
CHARACTERS = [
    # name, textures folder, mesh, metallic channel, roughness channel, neon glow
    ("Hero", "Art/Models/hero_fixed/textures", "/Game/Characters/Hero/SK_Hero", (0, 0, 1), (0, 1, 0), 3.0),
    ("Publisher", "Art/Models/boss_fixed/textures", "/Game/Characters/Publisher/SK_Publisher", (1, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 0.0),
]
MAPS = ["base_color", "normal", "metallic", "roughness"]

lib = unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary
tools = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()


def log(text):
    unreal.log("create_character_materials: " + text)


def import_texture(path, folder, name):
    task = unreal.AssetImportTask()
    task.set_editor_property("filename", os.path.join(ROOT, path))
    task.set_editor_property("destination_path", folder)
    task.set_editor_property("destination_name", name)
    task.set_editor_property("automated", True)
    task.set_editor_property("replace_existing", True)
    task.set_editor_property("save", False)
    tools.import_asset_tasks([task])
    texture = unreal.load_asset("%s/%s" % (folder, name))
    if name.endswith("_normal"):
        texture.set_editor_property("compression_settings", unreal.TextureCompressionSettings.TC_NORMALMAP)
        texture.set_editor_property("srgb", False)
    elif not name.endswith("_base_color"):
        texture.set_editor_property("compression_settings", unreal.TextureCompressionSettings.TC_MASKS)
        texture.set_editor_property("srgb", False)
    return texture


def node(mat, cls, x, y, **props):
    expr = lib.create_material_expression(mat, cls, x, y)
    for key, value in props.items():
        expr.set_editor_property(key, value)
    return expr


def mask(mat, source, x, y, r=False, g=False, b=False):
    m = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionComponentMask, x, y, r=r, g=g, b=b, a=False)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(source, "", m, "")
    return m


def binary(mat, cls, a, b, x, y):
    n = node(mat, cls, x, y)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(a, "", n, "A")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(b, "", n, "B")
    return n


def scalar(mat, name, value, x, y):
    return node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionScalarParameter, x, y, parameter_name=name, default_value=value)


def vector(mat, name, value, x, y):
    return node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionVectorParameter, x, y, parameter_name=name,
                default_value=unreal.LinearColor(*value))


def sample(mat, name, texture, sampler, x, y):
    return node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionTextureSampleParameter2D, x, y, parameter_name=name, texture=texture,
                sampler_type=sampler)


def channel(mat, texture_name, texture, channel_name, x, y):
    """dot(texture.rgb, channel.rgb): one channel of a mask texture, picked by a vector parameter."""
    tex = sample(mat, texture_name, texture, unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_MASKS, x, y)
    pick = mask(mat, vector(mat, channel_name, (1, 0, 0, 0), x, y + 220), x + 250, y + 220, True, True, True)
    rgb = mask(mat, tex, x + 250, y, True, True, True)
    return binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionDotProduct, rgb, pick, x + 450, y)


def build_master(textures):
    path = "%s/%s" % (FOLDER, MASTER)
    if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(path):
        mat = unreal.load_asset(path)
        lib.delete_all_material_expressions(mat)
    else:
        mat = tools.create_asset(MASTER, FOLDER, unreal.Material, unreal.MaterialFactoryNew())
    mat.set_editor_property("used_with_skeletal_mesh", True)

    base = sample(mat, "BaseColor", textures["base_color"], unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_COLOR, -1600, -400)
    base_rgb = mask(mat, base, -1350, -400, True, True, True)
    flash = scalar(mat, "Flash", 0.0, -1350, -250)
    flash_color = vector(mat, "FlashColor", (1, 1, 1, 1), -1350, -150)
    flash_rgb = mask(mat, flash_color, -1150, -150, True, True, True)
    color = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionLinearInterpolate, -800, -400)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(base_rgb, "", color, "A")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(flash_rgb, "", color, "B")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(flash, "", color, "Alpha")
    lib.connect_material_property(color, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_BASE_COLOR)

    normal = sample(mat, "Normal", textures["normal"], unreal.MaterialSamplerType.SAMPLERTYPE_NORMAL, -800, 0)
    lib.connect_material_property(normal, "RGB", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_NORMAL)
    metallic = channel(mat, "Metallic", textures["metallic"], "MetallicChannel", -1600, 250)
    lib.connect_material_property(metallic, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_METALLIC)
    rough = channel(mat, "Roughness", textures["roughness"], "RoughnessChannel", -1600, 600)
    lib.connect_material_property(rough, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_ROUGHNESS)

    # Neon: saturation = max(r, g, b) - min(r, g, b), ramped from NeonFrom over 1 / NeonSharp.
    r = mask(mat, base, -1350, -900, r=True)
    g = mask(mat, base, -1350, -820, g=True)
    b = mask(mat, base, -1350, -740, b=True)
    hi = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMax, r, binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMax, g, b, -1150, -800), -1000, -900)
    lo = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMin, r, binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMin, g, b, -1150, -700), -1000, -760)
    sat = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionSubtract, hi, lo, -850, -850)
    ramp = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply,
                  binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionSubtract, sat, scalar(mat, "NeonFrom", 0.35, -850, -700), -700, -850),
                  scalar(mat, "NeonSharp", 4.0, -700, -700), -550, -850)
    neon_mask = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionSaturate, -400, -850)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(ramp, "", neon_mask, "")
    neon = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply,
                  binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, base_rgb, neon_mask, -250, -850),
                  scalar(mat, "NeonGlow", 0.0, -250, -700), -100, -850)
    flash_light = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply,
                         binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, flash_rgb, flash, -800, -150),
                         scalar(mat, "FlashGlow", 2.0, -800, -60), -600, -150)
    emissive = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionAdd, neon, flash_light, 100, -500)
    lib.connect_material_property(emissive, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_EMISSIVE_COLOR)
    lib.recompile_material(mat)
    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mat, False)
    return mat


def build_instance(master, name, textures, metallic_channel, rough_channel, neon):
    path = "%s/MI_%s" % (FOLDER, name)
    if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(path):
        mi = unreal.load_asset(path)
    else:
        mi = tools.create_asset("MI_" + name, FOLDER, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstant, unreal.MaterialInstanceConstantFactoryNew())
    lib.set_material_instance_parent(mi, master)
    for param, key in (("BaseColor", "base_color"), ("Normal", "normal"), ("Metallic", "metallic"), ("Roughness", "roughness")):
        lib.set_material_instance_texture_parameter_value(mi, param, textures[key])
    lib.set_material_instance_vector_parameter_value(mi, "MetallicChannel", unreal.LinearColor(*metallic_channel, 0))
    lib.set_material_instance_vector_parameter_value(mi, "RoughnessChannel", unreal.LinearColor(*rough_channel, 0))
    lib.set_material_instance_scalar_parameter_value(mi, "NeonGlow", neon)
    lib.update_material_instance(mi)
    unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mi, False)
    return mi


master = None
for name, source, mesh_path, metallic_channel, rough_channel, neon in CHARACTERS:
    textures = {m: import_texture("%s/%s.png" % (source, m), "/Game/Characters/%s/Textures" % name, "T_%s_%s" % (name, m)) for m in MAPS}
    if master is None:
        master = build_master(textures)
    mi = build_instance(master, name, textures, metallic_channel, rough_channel, neon)
    mesh = unreal.load_asset(mesh_path)
    slots = mesh.get_editor_property("materials")
    for slot in slots:
        slot.set_editor_property("material_interface", mi)
    mesh.set_editor_property("materials", slots)
    log("%s: %d slot(s) wear %s" % (mesh_path, len(slots), mi.get_name()))
unreal.EditorLoadingAndSavingUtils.save_dirty_packages(True, True)
log("done")

"""
KIND: offline tool (headless Blender). Per clip of a character: the frame where a hand moves fastest, and where a hand
is lowest, as candidates for the impact frame the game times its hits by (JamFighterView clip table).

    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/clip_impacts.py -- <file.blend|.glb> [fps]
"""
import sys

import bpy

args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
source = args[0]
fps = float(args[1]) if len(args) > 1 else 30.0
scene = bpy.context.scene
scene.render.fps = int(fps)
if source.endswith(".blend"):
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=source)
else:
    bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=source)
arm = next(o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "ARMATURE")
HANDS = [b for b in ("hand_r", "hand_l") if b in arm.pose.bones]
for action in sorted(bpy.data.actions, key=lambda a: a.name):
    if not arm.animation_data:
        arm.animation_data_create()
    arm.animation_data.action = action
    if action.slots:
        arm.animation_data.action_slot = action.slots[0]
    first, last = (int(round(f)) for f in action.frame_range)
    track = {h: [] for h in HANDS}
    for frame in range(first, last + 1):
        scene.frame_set(frame)
        for h in HANDS:
            track[h].append((arm.matrix_world @ arm.pose.bones[h].head).copy())
    line = "%-26s %3d frames" % (action.name, last - first + 1)
    for h in HANDS:
        pts = track[h]
        speeds = [(pts[i + 1] - pts[i - 1]).length / 2 * fps for i in range(1, len(pts) - 1)]
        fast = max(range(len(speeds)), key=lambda i: speeds[i]) + 1
        low = min(range(len(pts)), key=lambda i: pts[i].z)
        line += " | %s fastest f%d (%.2f s, %.1f u/s) lowest f%d (%.2f s)" % (h, fast, fast / fps, speeds[fast - 1], low, low / fps)
    print("[impact] " + line)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Records a clip of the game playing itself: the bot drives the hero on the top-down camera.
#   demo_clip.sh [seconds] [output.mp4] [camera]
# camera: ignored since T-018 (only the top-down camera is left), kept so older calls still work.
# Opens a game window for the length of the clip plus the start-up: warn the author first.
# Extra game switches go in JAM_DEMO_ARGS, e.g. JAM_DEMO_ARGS=-JamDemoHoldUltimate (the bot never presses E).
# The game saves every frame as a PNG at a fixed 30 fps (see Source/JamGame/Public/Game/JamDemo.h), ffmpeg joins them.
set -u
UE="F:/Program Files/Epic Games/UE_5.8"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd -W)"
SECONDS_TO_RUN="${1:-26}"
OUT="${2:-$ROOT/Saved/Demo/demo_$(date +%m%d_%H%M).mp4}"
# A fresh folder per run: frames of an earlier run must never pad out a shorter one.

# T-060 His stolen shurikens never explode

**Block:** session 5, fight · **Status:** done

## Goal

The author on `session-5i` (Sat 14 Nov 19:50): when the Publisher steals the Shuriken he throws as often as now, but
none of his explode, and they are a little easier to parry with the strike (slower or a larger parry reach, the
agent's call). The hero's own "every third explodes" stays (the author's answer, same evening).

## Decision

A larger parry reach, the speed kept: his shurikens carry `BossShurikenParryMargin=30` (cm). While the parry is open,
one of his that passes within the hero's body plus 30 cm goes back, and the strike's look-ahead (T-044, T-057) sees it
from that far out. What goes back loses the margin. His shurikens were already 0.8 of the hero's speed (T-055).

## Test seam

`Jam.Shuriken.HisStolenOnesNeverExplode` (red first: 2 of 6 exploded, no margin), `Jam.Parry.HisShurikenIsCaughtFromFurtherOut`
(red first: passed by).

## As built

- `JamShurikenRules::Throw`: the boss's shot is never explosive and carries the margin. Not a zero in `[JamBalance]`:
  the validator reads every zero as a missing line.
- `FJamShot::ParryMargin`, `FJamProjectile::ParryMargin`; `AdvanceProjectiles` deflects on the wider sweep while the
  parry is open, `JamParryRules::ShotWithin` looks with it.
- The blast ring under his explosive shurikens (`JamFeedbackRules::ShowsBlastRing`) no longer has anything to show;
  left in place, its test still passes.


| Ticket | One line |
|---|---|
| [T-055](T-055_stolen_at_full_strength.md) | What he stole hits at full strength, a shorter pause (0.9 / x1 / 0.8 / 0.7) |
| [T-038](T-038_stolen_parry_and_ultimate.md) | His stolen Parry is a shield stance, his stolen Ultimate a timed locked line |
| [T-056](T-056_signature_combos.md) | A signature combo per stolen mechanic |
| [T-057](T-057_parry_buffer.md) | An early parry click waits for the shot (0.3 s look-ahead) |
| [T-058](T-058_ultimate_turns.md) | The Ultimate turns toward the cursor during its wind-up, 120 deg/s |

## Saturday night: feedback on session-5i, then the models (the author, Sat 14 Nov 19:50)

| Ticket | One line |
|---|---|
| [T-059](T-059_parry_rearm.md) | A good parry is ready again at once: spamming LMB sends back every shot of a burst (done) |
| [T-060](T-060_his_shurikens_plain.md) | His stolen shurikens never explode, the parry catches them 30 cm further out (done) |

# T-061 The 3D hero and Publisher replace the stand-ins

**Block:** session 5, models · **Status:** done

## Goal

The author, Sun 15 Nov 00:30: the approved models go into the game now. The hero (Meshy model, rig and clips) and
the Publisher (the rebuilt rig of `Art/Models/boss_fixed`, seventh export) replace the shapes; the bean, the T-pose
and the other cosmetic layers keep working; the Publisher is 2.6 m to the hero's 1.8 m; the travel of
`Hit_Reaction`, `Knock_Down` and `Kung_Fu_Punch` is locked on the root.

## Decision

- **The hero is exported like the Publisher** (`Tools/Art/hero_export.py`, Blender): one mesh FBX in centimetres and
  one FBX per clip. A `root` bone is added under `pelvis`, and in `Hit_Reaction`, `Dead` and `Roll_Dodge` the
  horizontal travel of the hips moves to it, so Force Root Lock keeps him in place while the hips still drop. The
  merged Meshy clip file gave Unreal only one of its seven takes.
- **No animation blueprint.** `UJamPoseInstance` blends by hand in C++ (its proxy's `Evaluate`): the idle, the walk
  by the speed, and one action over them, from `spine_01` up while he walks, the whole body when he stands or the
  action says so. The T-pose layer is the reference pose.
- **The simulation sets the timing.** `JamPoseRules::CueFor` picks the clip from the step's events (strike, guard,
  slam circles, throws, Ultimate, hits, the stun); `Fit` starts and speeds the clip so its impact frame (measured
  with `Tools/Art/clip_impacts.py`) shows on the step the blow lands. The Publisher staggers only under hits of 25
  and more, a hit never cuts a strike or a guard.
- **One material for both** (`M_JamCharacter`): the Meshy textures, a white flash for hits, and the saturated parts
  of the base colour glow (the hero's piping), switched off with the effects layer. Albedo is scaled to 0.3 for the
  scene's locked exposure.
- **Kung_Fu_Punch** stays out of the fight (it belongs to the intro, T-030).

## Test seam

`Jam.Pose.*` (9 tests, red first against a stub): the strike and its lead, the second slash, the guard by the
window, the slam on its first new circle, his throws and his Ultimate, hits by weight and the stun, the priority of
a step, who lies down, `Fit`, the fades. The look is checked from the game camera in `Clips/t061_models_in_game.mp4`
(`-JamDemoSkipEvery=10`: the glow, the grid, the T-pose and the bean on the 3D hero).

## As built

- Import: `Tools/Editor/import_models.py` (classic FBX importer, GLB through Interchange),
  `create_character_materials.py` (textures from `Tools/Art/save_textures.py`), `report_models.py`.
- `AJamFighterView`: the skeletal model, the katana in `hand_r`, the bean kept; `Act` starts the cues.
- `/Game/Characters` and `/Game/Props` are always cooked: the views load them by path.
- Known: the Publisher's walk is played at up to 3.5 times its speed and still slides (he moves 6 times faster than
  the clip). The FBX importer also left `*.fbm` texture folders next to the sources and two assets of the first
  try (`/Game/Props/model_glb`, `result_animation_fbx_url_Roll_Dodge`); none is committed.

content.thinking: I'm setting up the card material first, with the round-5 textures for the memos and bills, and the cash-stack model for the heal. The shuriken keeps its team colours through the neon material.

input.content:
"""Creates the material of the paper props (T-062): the Publisher's memos and the dollar bills. Runs inside the editor,
headless, after import_models.py:

UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe JamGame.uproject -run=pythonscript -script="Tools/Editor/create_card_material.py"

M_JamCard is unlit and two-sided: Card (the texture) times Color times Glow, so a Glow above 1 blooms like the neon of
the stand-ins. MI_MemoCard and MI_DollarCard carry the round-5 textures. Running it again rebuilds them.
"""
import unreal

FOLDER = "/Game/Props/Materials"
MASTER = "M_JamCard"
CARDS = [("MI_MemoCard", "/Game/Props/Textures/T_MemoCard"), ("MI_DollarCard", "/Game/Props/Textures/T_DollarCard")]

lib = unreal.MaterialEditingLibrary
tools = unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools()


def log(text):
    unreal.log("create_card_material: " + text)


def node(mat, cls, x, y, **props):
    expr = lib.create_material_expression(mat, cls, x, y)
    for key, value in props.items():
        expr.set_editor_property(key, value)
    return expr


def binary(mat, cls, a, b, x, y):
    n = node(mat, cls, x, y)
    lib.connect_material_expressions(a, "", n, "A")
    lib.connect_material_expressions(b, "", n, "B")
    return n


path = "%s/%s" % (FOLDER, MASTER)
if unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.does_asset_exist(path):
    mat = unreal.load_asset(path)
    lib.delete_all_material_expressions(mat)
else:
    mat = tools.create_asset(MASTER, FOLDER, unreal.Material, unreal.MaterialFactoryNew())
mat.set_editor_property("shading_model", unreal.MaterialShadingModel.MSM_UNLIT)
mat.set_editor_property("two_sided", True)
first = unreal.load_asset(CARDS[0][1])
card = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionTextureSampleParameter2D, -900, 0, parameter_name="Card", texture=first)
rgb = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionComponentMask, -650, 0, r=True, g=True, b=True, a=False)
lib.connect_material_expressions(card, "", rgb, "")
color = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionVectorParameter, -900, 250, parameter_name="Color",
             default_value=unreal.LinearColor(1, 1, 1, 1))
color_rgb = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionComponentMask, -650, 250, r=True, g=True, b=True, a=False)
lib.connect_material_expressions(color, "", color_rgb, "")
glow = node(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionScalarParameter, -650, 400, parameter_name="Glow", default_value=1.0)
lit = binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, binary(mat, unreal.MaterialExpressionMultiply, rgb, color_rgb, -450, 100), glow, -250, 200)
lib.connect_material_property(lit, "", unreal.MaterialProperty.MP_EMISSIVE_COLOR)
lib.recompile_material(mat)
unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_loaded_asset(mat, False)

# T-062 The generated props replace the greybox shapes

**Block:** session 5, models · **Status:** done

## Goal

The author, Sun 15 Nov 00:30: the approved props go into the game with the characters. The shuriken, the cash
stack, the paper dollar and the memo card replace their greybox shapes; the katana is already in the hero's hand
(T-061).

## Decision

- **Shuriken:** the Hunyuan3D model, laid flat and spinning, worn in the neon of its side (the hero's cyan, the
  Publisher's red, explosive yellow): whose it is and whether it explodes must read at a glance, so the colour stays
  the code's, the shape is the model's.
- **Memo and bill:** cards in `M_JamCard` (unlit, two-sided, texture times colour times glow) with the round-5
  textures `r5_memo_card` and `r5_dollar_card`.
- **Cash stack (the heal of T-049):** the model with its own textures, 90 cm long, still bobbing and turning, the
  pulsing ring kept. It has its own small pool in the effects view: the neon pool repaints everything it hands out.
- **The hit flash of the characters** was turned down (FlashGlow 2 to 0.4): the Publisher is hit all the time and
  read as a white shape for whole seconds.

## Test seam

Presentation only, no new decision: checked from the game camera in the clip of the milestone. The 218 `Jam.` tests
stay green.

## As built

- `Tools/Editor/create_card_material.py`; `JamShapes::Shuriken`, `CashStack`, `MemoCard`, `DollarCard`, `Card`.
- `AJamProjectilesView` (shuriken, memo), `AJamMoneyView` (bills; its unused glow parameter removed),
  `AJamEffectsView::DrawCash`.
- A unity-build clash of names from T-061 fixed on the way (`StaggerHit`, `MinClipRate`, `MaxClipRate`).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Packages the jam project for Win64 into Saved/Packaged/Windows and zips it next to the folder.
#   package.sh [--config Development|Shipping] [--name ZipBaseName] [--no-zip]
# Builds from the working tree. The editor can stay open: only the game target is compiled.
# The submission zip must be named TeamName_GameName: pass it with --name.
set -u
UE="F:/Program Files/Epic Games/UE_5.8"
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd -W)"
OUT="$ROOT/Saved/Packaged"
LOG="$ROOT/Saved/BuildCycle/package_$(date +%H%M%S).log"
CONFIG=Development
NAME=""
DO_ZIP=1
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
	case "$1" in
		--config) shift; CONFIG="$1" ;;
		--name) shift; NAME="$1" ;;
		--no-zip) DO_ZIP=0 ;;
	esac
	shift
done
[ -z "$NAME" ] && NAME="JamGame_$CONFIG"

mkdir -p "$OUT" "$ROOT/Saved/BuildCycle"
echo "[package] $CONFIG, log: $LOG"
"$UE/Engine/Build/BatchFiles/RunUAT.bat" BuildCookRun -project="$ROOT/JamGame.uproject" -noP4 -platform=Win64 -clientconfig="$CONFIG" \
	-build -cook -stage -pak -prereqs -archive -archivedirectory="$OUT" -nocompileeditor -ubtargs=-WaitMutex -unattended -utf8output >"$LOG" 2>&1
CODE=$?
grep -E "BUILD SUCCESSFUL|BUILD FAILED|AutomationTool exiting|Error:" "$LOG" | tail -12
if [ "$CODE" != 0 ]; then
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pushes a packaged folder to the itch page pavyny/neon-ronin, channel windows. Key from .env, never printed.
#   itch_push.sh <folder> <version>     e.g. itch_push.sh Saved/Packaged/Windows block-d
# Needs butler in ~/bin (v15.32.0 installed Sat 14 Nov). Pipe the output through a filter before showing it.
set -euo pipefail
cd /f/Unreal_Engine/UnrealProjects/MegaJam2026
BUTLER_API_KEY="$(grep '^BUTLER_API_KEY=' .env | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '\r"')"
export BUTLER_API_KEY
~/bin/butler.exe push "$1" pavyny/neon-ronin:windows --userversion "$2"
~/bin/butler.exe status pavyny/neon-ronin

input.content:
"""
KIND: offline tool (headless Blender). Renders a model's base colour flat (no light) from four sides, for checking
a texture: front, right, back, left side by side in one PNG. Optional third argument: a base-colour PNG to put on
the model instead of its own (to compare a repainted texture).

    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/flat_views.py -- <model.glb> <out.png> [base_color.png]
"""
import math
import os
import sys

import bpy
from mathutils import Vector

args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
src, out = args[0], args[1]
swap = args[2] if len(args) > 2 else None
for ob in list(bpy.data.objects):
    bpy.data.objects.remove(ob)
bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf(filepath=src)
meshes = [o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH" and o.parent is not None]
if swap:
    image = bpy.data.images.load(swap)
    for mesh in meshes:
        for slot in mesh.material_slots:
            for node in slot.material.node_tree.nodes:
                if node.type == "TEX_IMAGE" and node.image and "base" in node.image.name.lower():
                    node.image = image
scene = bpy.context.scene
scene.render.engine = "BLENDER_WORKBENCH"
scene.display.shading.light = "FLAT"
scene.display.shading.color_type = "TEXTURE"
scene.render.resolution_x, scene.render.resolution_y = 700, 1100
scene.render.film_transparent = False
scene.world = bpy.data.worlds.new("w") if not scene.world else scene.world
scene.display.shading.background_type = "VIEWPORT"
bpy.context.view_layer.update()
pts = [m.matrix_world @ Vector(c) for m in meshes for c in m.bound_box]
lo = Vector((min(p.x for p in pts), min(p.y for p in pts), min(p.z for p in pts)))
hi = Vector((max(p.x for p in pts), max(p.y for p in pts), max(p.z for p in pts)))
centre = (lo + hi) / 2
cam_data = bpy.data.cameras.new("cam")
cam_data.type = "ORTHO"
cam_data.ortho_scale = (hi.z - lo.z) * 1.05
cam = bpy.data.objects.new("cam", cam_data)
scene.collection.objects.link(cam)
scene.camera = cam
frames = []
# glTF forward is +Y after import into Blender's Z-up? The model faces -Y: front camera sits at -Y.
for name, yaw in (("front", 0), ("right", 90), ("back", 180), ("left", 270)):
    a = math.radians(yaw)
    d = 10.0
    cam.location = centre + Vector((d * math.sin(a), -d * math.cos(a), 0))
    cam.rotation_euler = (math.radians(90), 0, a)
    path = out.replace(".png", "_%s.png" % name)
    scene.render.filepath = path
    bpy.ops.render.render(write_still=True)
    frames.append(path)
print("[views] " + " ".join(frames))
